conventions.convention: The normal cone is outward: n belongs to N_C(x) precisely when ⟨n,z−x⟩≤0 for every z∈C; it is empty outside C. Dynamics satisfy f−ẋ∈N_C(x).
Vector absolute continuity is coordinatewise; the inclusion must hold outside one Lebesgue-null exceptional set where all coordinate derivatives exist.
Existence and convergence assume d≥1, T>0, nonempty compact convex C, joint time/state Lipschitz forcing, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice.
A projection certificate requires feasibility and supremum variational residual at most ε²; its resulting distance tolerance is ε.
The scalar procedure returns at its first impact, includes immediate incoming contact at time zero, uses e∈[0,1], and certifies whole-step nonpenetration before reporting free flight.
The binary normal points from sphere 2 to sphere 1; incoming relative normal velocity is negative, and positive impulse adds Jn/m₁ to velocity 1 and subtracts Jn/m₂ from velocity 2.

Sphere event times are reported at bracket upper endpoints. Bracket width and guard residual have separate tolerances; reset errors compare aligned states and include outgoing flow during the reporting lag.
Sphere guard, normal and reset bounds use the Euclidean norm of the full position/velocity state. The full-state normal bound includes a factor √2.

load_bearing.statement: For nonempty closed convex C⊆Rᵈ, d≥1, projected dynamics satisfy f(t,x(t))−ẋ(t)∈N_C(x(t)) almost everywhere, and exact Euler nodes satisfy x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)).
For d∈N, including d=0, and nonempty closed convex C⊆Rᵈ, ‖P_C(u)−P_C(v)‖₂≤‖u−v‖₂ for all u,v∈Rᵈ.

For d≥1, nonempty compact convex C, T>0, x₀∈C and forcing satisfying ‖f(t,x)−f(s,y)‖₂≤L(|t−s|+‖x−y‖₂), Countable Choice and Dependent Choice imply a unique absolutely continuous projected solution; the exact Euler affine interpolants converge uniformly to it.
For nonempty closed convex C⊆Rᵈ, including d=0, if p∈C and sup_{z∈C}⟨y−p,z−p⟩≤ε² with ε≥0, then ‖p−P_C(y)‖₂≤ε.
For nonempty closed convex C with the stated outward normal-cone convention, N_C is maximal monotone and, for every τ>0 and y, the unique p satisfying y−p∈τN_C(p) is P_C(y).

For d≥1, T>0, nonempty compact closed C⊆Rᵈ and M≥0, every sequence u_j:[0,T]→C with common Lipschitz constant M has a uniformly convergent subsequence whose limit lies in C and has the same Lipschitz bound.

At an isolated incoming binary sphere contact with positive masses/radii and e∈[0,1], J=−(1+e)v_n/(1/m₁+1/m₂)>0 gives conserved linear momentum, post-impact relative normal velocity −e v_n, unchanged tangential velocities and energy change −(1−e²)v_n²/[2(1/m₁+1/m₂)].

For two full states with pair distances at least σ>0 and relative speeds at most V≥0, the sphere guard is √2-Lipschitz, the normal is 2√2/σ-Lipschitz, and the extended reset is L_R-Lipschitz with L_R=1+√2 βκ(1+4V/σ). These endpoint bounds require no convex collision-free set.

concerns.concern: Provider requirement 3 permits a bracket [a,b] without requiring a<b. Requirement 4 then attributes its event-time bound to lem-transverse-hybrid-event-time-error, whose current Statement explicitly requires a<b. Singleton exact brackets, including [0,0] for an initial impact, need a separate zero-lag justification. The bound is immediate because τ=b in that case, but the cited lemma does not cover it.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 sets “R=‖x−c₀‖₂” and then uses “K=C∩\overline B(x,R)”. If x=c₀, R=0. The published def-metric-ball explicitly permits ball notation only for strictly positive radii and says a ball of radius zero is never written in this library. Thus this boundary case uses notation outside its declared domain. The underlying nearest-point claim remains valid.

seams_checked.note: The supplier's outward inequality ⟨n,z−x⟩≤0 agrees with the local cone and f−ẋ inclusion. No multiplier necessity or constraint-qualification conclusion is imported.
The indicator and zero-subdifferential definitions give ∂ι_C=N_C. The proximal suppliers apply to nonempty closed convex C and positive τ, yielding the unique projection resolvent with the same sign.

Orientation −1, uniform transversality, dense-error inflation, reset lag and common-mode flow estimates agree with the suppliers. One boundary mismatch remains: the consumer permits singleton event brackets, while its cited transverse-time lemma requires a<b. The zero-lag bound is elementary but needs separate treatment, as recorded in concerns.
